newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says has no comment on ex-MOF official remark.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says has no comment on ex-MOF official remark.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) does not comment on remarks by individuals referring to its monetary policy, a BOJ spokesman told Reuters on Thursday.
He was speaking after a Finance Ministry official said on Wednesday that the central bank was keen to change the official discount rate as soon as possible.
"As for the BOJ's monetary policy, please refer to remarks by governor (Yasuo) Matsushita at the latest news conference on Monday," he said.
Matsushita said on Monday that the BOJ's monetary policy is aimed at ensuring a basis for economic recovery.

Former Japanese vice finance minister for international affairs Makoto Utsumi told a symposium in Sydney on Wednesday that Matsushita is seeking to make an upward correction as soon as possible to the official discount rate, now standing at an extremely low level of 0.5 percent.
His remarks were carried on Thursday by a Japanese financial daily which is widely read by traders, and pushed down Japanese government bond prices.
In a separate interview on Wednesday with Reuters Financial Television, Utsumi said the BOJ wants to normalise the discount rate but is cautious.
Utsumi told RFTV the BOJ regarded the current level of the discount rate as "a bit abnormal".

"They understand that if they change it, it might have a very important impact on the Japanese economy. They are also cautious in changing it," he said. "I think as Mr. Matsushita has repeatedly said, he wants to see if Japan's economy is fully supported by private sector activity."
